method: Web research 2026-10-15 from search-engine summaries of the cited pages (pages not opened directly). Verify specific numbers before relying on them.
overview: Ernst & Young US is a Big Four firm. Its consulting practice covers business, technology and people consulting; the US early-careers board scanned here carries its campus and new-grad roles across service lines. Strategy and transactions sit in EY-Parthenon (profiled separately).
business_type: Big Four professional services (assurance, tax, consulting, strategy and transactions)
service_lines: Assurance incl. climate change and sustainability services

differentiators.text: EY runs its own credential programs: EY Badges (digital skills credentials, e.g. data and AI) and a free, accredited corporate Tech MBA with Hult International Business School open regardless of role.
differentiators.significance: A distinctive, firm-funded route to formal qualifications for someone not planning a graduate degree.

differentiators.text: In 2025 EY reorganised from 18 regions into 10 'super regions' after its 2023 plan to split consulting from audit (Project Everest) was abandoned.
differentiators.significance: The firm stayed integrated; consulting and audit remain one organisation.

early_career.text: EY reports US$385m spent on formal training in 2023 (global figure) and links badges to on-the-job experience, not only courses.
early_career.significance: Training spend is global, not specific to US new hires.

employee_support.text: In 2016 EY US announced up to 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents (after a year of service) and up to $25,000 per family for adoption, fertility treatment and surrogacy.
employee_support.significance: Dated announcements; confirm current terms with a recruiter.

employee_support.text: Third-party summaries describe flexible vacation, ~19 paid holidays including week-long summer and winter breaks, and up to 80 hours a year of paid family-care time.
employee_support.significance: Not confirmed on an EY page; summaries also conflict on the size of the well-being fund.

flexibility.text: EY has had a formal US flexibility leader and framed flexibility as firm policy since at least 2014 (Senate testimony).
flexibility.significance: Old evidence of intent, not of current team practice.

tradeoffs.text: 2025 restructuring removed layers of middle management; reported job cuts were concentrated outside the US, with US specifics unconfirmed.
tradeoffs.significance: Ask how the restructuring changed the team you would join.

tradeoffs.text: Summaries note that taking time off can be hard in busy periods despite generous stated leave.
tradeoffs.significance: Policy and practice may differ by team and season.

unknowns: Current US parental-leave and well-being-fund terms (sources are dated or conflict).
Typical hours and travel for NYC consulting staff.
